llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (passive detection of skill-crawling) is generally coherent, but there are notable inconsistencies and a possible data‑exfil surface (alerts -> webhooks) that you should verify before installing.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md describes a passive detector that only needs read access to request metadata and alert-sending capability — this aligns with the stated anti-crawler purpose. No binaries, env vars, or installs are required, which is proportionate. Minor mismatch: the platform-level manifest (provided metadata) doesn't list requested permissions, while SKILL.md lists 'request_metadata_read' and 'alert_send'; that should be reconciled with the platform's permission model.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions claim strictly read-only analysis and explicitly say they do NOT access caller IPs or response content, yet the detection rules include 'session_fingerprint_anomaly' and 'user-agent' analysis which commonly rely on header/session identifiers and sometimes IP correlation. Also the configuration allows alert channels including 'webhook' and 'email' — sending structured alerts to external endpoints is an outbound data flow that could leak request-metadata unless the operator tightly controls the endpoint and alert contents. The SKILL.md does not clearly enumerate exactly which metadata fields will be included in alerts.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec or code files — minimal installation risk because nothing is downloaded or written to disk by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or external credentials. The only privileges it asks for (in SKILL.md) are request_metadata_read and alert_send, which are reasonable for detection+alerting. Confirm that those platform permissions are narrowly scoped and do not expose sensitive identifiers.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill manifest in SKILL.md sets autonomous: false and notes operator invocation only, but the registry metadata supplied to this review shows disable-model-invocation: false (platform default). This mismatch is important: confirm with the platform whether the skill can be auto-invoked or forced into agent workflows. always: false (no permanent forced inclusion) is appropriate.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing: 1) Confirm with the platform which permissions the skill will actually be granted (does request_metadata_read include IPs, session IDs, user-agent, cookies, etc.?). 2) Verify whether the platform will allow autonomous invocation despite SKILL.md claiming 'autonomous: false' — if autonomous invocation is possible, the detector could run without your explicit action. 3) If you plan to enable non-default alert channels (webhook/email), review what exact metadata will be sent in alerts and only point alerts at trusted endpoints; treat webhooks as potential exfil targets. 4) Ask the publisher to clarify which metadata fields are used for detection and which fields appear in alerts (sample alert schema). 5) If you need more assurance, run the skill in a controlled/test environment or request source code/implementation details so you can confirm it truly never reads response bodies or PII. If the publisher cannot reconcile the autonomy/permission mismatches or provide clear alert schemas, consider this skill untrusted.
